memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Eat them as you would gazelle or deer. Both the ceremonially unclean and the clean may eat. But be sure you do not eat the blood, because the blood is the life, and you must not eat the life with the meat. You must not eat the blood; pour it out on the ground like water. Do not eat it, so that it may go well with you and your children after you, because you will be doing what is right in the eyes of the Lord. - Deut 12:22-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Once more God underscores the command about blood: "the blood is the life." This repetition shows how important the principle was. Life is a sacred thing, given by God, and the blood — representing life — was to be treated with reverence, poured out rather than consumed. God was training His people to hold life as holy and to remember that atonement is costly. Obedience here was tied to doing "what is right in the eyes of the Lord."

The deeper we look, the more we see how this points to Christ. All this reverence for blood, all these repeated reminders that "the blood is the life," prepared God's people to understand the infinite value of the blood Jesus would shed. His life, poured out on the cross, is the ultimate atonement. The lifeblood of the Son of God was the price of our redemption — a truth so weighty that the old covenant spent centuries teaching the people to revere blood so they might grasp it.

Notice too the phrase "so that it may go well with you." In its covenant setting, obedience in the land brought God's blessing. We should not turn this into a guarantee that obedient believers today always have smooth lives — that would twist the text. But the enduring truth is that walking in obedience to God, doing what is right in His eyes, is always good for us and honors Him. And our confidence rests not in our perfect obedience but in Christ, whose blood makes us right with God. Revere the life He poured out, and walk in glad obedience as those redeemed at such cost.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- How does the repeated reverence for blood deepen my understanding of Christ's sacrifice?
- Do I hold life as sacred, as God does?
- How does resting in Christ's blood free me to walk in glad obedience?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, all this reverence for blood points me to the infinite value of the blood Jesus shed for me. Help me hold life as sacred and never take His sacrifice lightly. Thank You that His blood makes me right with You, freeing me to walk in glad obedience. Amen.
